title: Circuit-bypass proxy and degraded-read operational mode for dependency failures
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Problem: During regional downstream outages (Redis/Kafka/primary DB), the serving runtime is currently either blocking requests while connections drain or returning hard errors that spike client-side latency and create cascading retries. We need a low-risk operational mode that keeps the platform within user-facing SLOs by offering a degraded but useful response path: 1) short-circuiting synchronous calls with a proxy shim that implements circuit-bypass rules and tenant-aware eviction, 2) serving stale-or-local-cache reads with bounded staleness guarantees, and 3) draining/purging ephemeral connection leases to avoid connection pileups. Goal: implement a circuit-bypass proxy + degraded-read mode that buys time during dependency disruption without violating data-safety constraints or dramatically increasing error budgets.
acceptance_criteria: New proxy shim (bypass-proxy) routes dependent calls and exposes a simple policy interface: allow / soft-evict / passthrough
Degraded-read mode returns cached or stale reads for keys with staleness <= configured window (default 30s), with explicit response header 'X-RI-Degraded: true'
Connection lease system added to connpool: ephemeral leases expire after X ms and can be forcibly released via API; recent leak scenarios reproduce fixed in unit tests
SLOs preserved: 99th percentile P95 request latency during simulated downstream partial outage degrades no more than 2x baseline and error-rate remains under defined target for canary tenants
End-to-end automated tests (integration + load) and a Grafana dashboard showing degradation state, stale-hit rate, and per-tenant fallback counts
Design doc and security review approved for stale-read use cases and tenant opt-out mechanism
decisions: Use a lightweight proxy shim colocated with the runtime (same pod) rather than a central proxy to reduce cross-region fanout and make policy enforcement tenant-local
Stale-read window defaults to 30s but is configurable per-tenant and per-route; write operations are never served from stale-cache
Circuit-bypass uses a graded scoring model: SuccessLatencyScore + ErrorRate + ConnLeasePressure -> if above threshold, route to degraded-policy
Expose per-tenant opt-out via config in the control plane (Private/Dedicated customers can disable degraded reads)
Avoid strong data consistency guarantees for degraded mode; document clearly and include automatic telemetry to surface data-sensitivity risks
implementation_notes: Bypass-proxy will implement three actions for each dependency call: PASSTHROUGH, SOFT_EVICT (short-circuit to cache or fallback), FAILFAST
Connpool changes: introduce EphemeralLease object tracked in hot path with fast-path atomic allocation and cooperative release hook on request completion
Policy engine uses rolling 60s window to compute scores; tunables exposed via runtime flags and control-plane overrides
Instrumentation: counters for degraded decisions, histogram for stale age, gauge for ephemeral leases in-use, and trace annotations for fallback paths
Add integration harness that can pause a downstream (iptables DROP) and assert responses, latency and telemetry collection
testing_plan: Unit tests for EphemeralLease allocation/release including race and forced-release paths
Component tests for proxy shim behaviour under synthetic latency and error induction
Chaos test: two-region failure simulation with 10k RPS traffic to validate per-tenant SLO preservation and graceful recovery
Security test to ensure stale reads never return PII for routes marked 'no-stale' (control-plane marker)
Canary rollout to 5% of non-production tenants, monitor for 48h before expanding to 25%
rollout_plan: Phase 1: merge feature-gate behind runtime flag and control-plane toggle; unit + integration tests green. Phase 2: enable in staging for all services and run chaos tests. Phase 3: canary to 5% internal/non-prod tenants for 48h. Phase 4: enable 25% external free-tier tenants. Phase 5: full enable for tenants without opt-out. Monitor metrics and rollback switch if error-rate + stale-hit exceed thresholds.
risks: Data correctness: stale reads may surface stale data for critical routes — mitigated by control-plane no-stale flag and opt-out
Operational complexity: more runtime flags and per-tenant tuning increases configuration surface — mitigated by sane defaults and central templates
Observability gaps: if telemetry is incomplete, we may not detect silent degradation — mitigated by adding explicit dashboards and alerts
Security review: some enterprises will reject any stale-read mechanism — mitigation: make opt-out trivial and document KMS/auditing scope
comments: 2026-02-19 - Aisha Banerjee: Initial triage completed. We have two concrete approaches: (A) proxy shim + per-tenant cache policy, (B) aggressive connpool admission with priority lanes. Team leans to (A) as lower-risk for existing traffic patterns.

2026-02-24 - Design review (Leah Morgan, Samir Desai): Request clarifications on stale-read opt-out UX and metrics. Action: add 'X-RI-Degraded' response header and control-plane toggle. Leah asked for explicit list of sensitive routes.

2026-02-28 - Tomás Ortega: Prototype implemented a colocated bypass-proxy and EphemeralLease. Local perf shows negligible median latency change; P95 increases by 6% under no-failure. Under injected Redis 200ms latency, degraded decision triggers and stale-hits at ~18% of reads.

2026-03-03 - Security review kickoff: security asked for confirmation that stale cache TTLs are auditable and that private deployment customers can disable the feature. Security review marked required and added checklist.
2026-03-05 - Tomás Ortega: PRs opened for runtime and control-plane. Requesting review from infra and SRE. Canary schedule proposed: start 2026-03-18 on non-prod tenants.
